name: SIP — first deployment

spent.note: The deployer EOA and the two bootstrap contracts are all spent. Verified on chain: the deployer holds NO role on the timelock and owns nothing; the bootstraps revoked their own roles at block 57746449. Nothing needs the deployer key again.

governance.note: A HOT KEY, generated for testing. It is proposer, executor, canceller, guardian and fee owner. The timelock is what makes moving this to hardware a grant-then-revoke batch rather than a redeploy.
governance.walletPolicy: TWO wallets for this phase, deliberately. The governor holds every operational role there is — timelock proposer/executor/canceller, FeeController owner, PauseController guardian, AdapterRegistry guardian — so it is deployer, governor and guardian in one. The attester is the second, and it never needs gas: it signs the attestation, while the settle transaction is sent by the trading wallet through its Privy seat. Any third address is an accident to be swept and forgotten.

notReadyFor: invest(): the AdapterRegistry is empty, so no vault can invest until governance registers an adapter
anyone else's money: the governor is a hot key and the delay is zero
